sources.locator: §1.1.3, PDF pp.39–40 (printed pp.31–32), Schmidt decompositions; §§2.1.2–2.1.3, PDF pp.69–80 (printed pp.61–72), states, ensembles, partial trace and purifications; §2.3.1, PDF pp.109–110 (printed pp.101–102), finite positive measurement families.
sources.reading_verification: I inspected the cached full-text sections §1.1.3, §§2.1.2–2.1.3, and §2.3.1. Each cited mathematical statement is reconstructed with a complete local proof; source formulations involving measurement semantics are not adopted.

contents.name: Density operator
contents.support: §2.1.2 identifies density operators as positive semidefinite trace-one operators; the local definition also defines support and faithfulness and excludes the zero space.

contents.name: Finite positive effect family
contents.support: §2.3.1 defines a finite family of positive measurement operators summing to identity; the local definition states the underlying algebraic data without adopting a measurement law.

contents.name: Pure state and ray
contents.support: §2.1.2 identifies pure states with normalized rank-one projectors and vectors modulo unit phase; the local definition uses the repository linear-first convention.

contents.name: A complete positive family consists of effects
contents.support: From the positive-family identity in §2.3.1, the complement of a member is the sum of the other positive terms; the finite-sum proof, including one outcome, is local.

contents.name: Every nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space admits a density operator
contents.support: §2.1.2 gives the completely mixed state I/d; the local proof verifies positivity and trace for every nonzero finite-dimensional H.

contents.name: Ray-to-projector is well-defined and bijective
contents.support: §2.1.2 relates unit vectors modulo phase to rank-one projectors; the local proof establishes both directions, positivity, and trace.

contents.name: Schmidt decomposition
contents.support: §1.1.3 derives Schmidt form from the singular value decomposition; the local proof fixes the second-factor conjugation for the repository convention.

contents.name: Ensemble and purification
contents.support: §§2.1.2–2.1.3 define finite state ensembles and vector purifications; the local definition fixes zero-weight components and finite auxiliary spaces.

contents.name: Density operators have an orthogonal spectral ensemble
contents.support: §2.1.2 gives the spectral mixture of a density operator; the local proof omits zero eigenvalues and identifies the number of terms with rank.

contents.name: Finite ensemble barycenters are density operators
contents.support: §2.1.2 states convex combinations of density operators remain density operators; the local proof includes zero weights and block regrouping.

contents.name: Every finite state ensemble is obtainable from a purification
contents.support: The source develops finite ensembles, effects, and purifications; its statements do not supply the grouped mixed-component square-root-filter identity, which is proved locally.

contents.name: Purifications exist and are unitarily equivalent after padding
contents.support: §2.1.3, Theorems 2.10–2.12, gives the rank criterion and unitary equivalence; the local proof handles arbitrary specified embeddings and repeated eigenvalues.

contents.name: Rank-one density operators are pure-state projectors
contents.support: §2.1.2 identifies pure states with rank-one density operators; the local proof normalizes the unique spectral weight and proves ray uniqueness.

contents.name: The set of density operators is convex
contents.support: §2.1.2 states convexity of density operators; the local proof proves positivity and trace via the finite barycenter supplier.

contents.name: The least purification environment dimension is the density rank
contents.support: Theorem 2.10 gives the rank threshold for purification; the local proof derives the lower bound for every finite auxiliary space and attains it.

sources.reading_verification: I inspected the complete text of the relevant passages in Chapter 2: §§2.3, 2.4, 2.5.1–2.5.2, and 2.5.5. Preskill’s physical postulates are not used; the mathematical interfaces and proof caveats are recorded item by item.

contents.name: Density operator
contents.support: §2.3 defines subsystem density operators and partial-trace reductions; local scope excludes physical postulates.

contents.name: Pure state and ray
contents.support: §2.3 distinguishes pure states from mixed density operators and records phase-equivalent unit representatives.

contents.name: Every nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space admits a density operator
contents.support: §2.3 gives normalized density operators, including a maximally mixed example; the general I/d verification is local.

contents.name: Ray-to-projector is well-defined and bijective
contents.support: §2.3 explains phase invariance of the rank-one projector; injectivity and the full bijection are proved locally.

contents.name: Schmidt decomposition
contents.support: §2.4 derives Schmidt form for a bipartite pure state and relates the coefficients to singular values.

contents.name: Ensemble and purification
contents.support: §§2.5.1–2.5.2 and §2.5.5 describe ensembles and purifications; the local definition fixes finite and zero-weight conventions.

contents.name: Density operators have an orthogonal spectral ensemble
contents.support: §2.5.1 uses diagonalization to express density operators as convex sums of pure states; zero eigenvalues are omitted locally.

contents.name: Finite ensemble barycenters are density operators
contents.support: §2.5.1 proves convexity and §2.5.2 discusses ensemble averages; the local proof also treats zero-total blocks.

contents.name: Every finite state ensemble is obtainable from a purification
contents.support: §2.5.5 proves the HJW correspondence for pure-state ensembles; the local argument proves the stronger grouped mixed-component identity for arbitrary purifications.

contents.name: Purifications exist and are unitarily equivalent after padding
contents.support: §2.5.5 relates purifications of the same density operator by an auxiliary unitary; the local proof handles arbitrary dimensions and embeddings.

contents.name: Rank-one density operators are pure-state projectors
contents.support: §2.3 identifies pure projectors; the local proof derives the rank-one converse with its trace normalization.

contents.name: The set of density operators is convex
contents.support: §2.5.1 explicitly proves convexity, including endpoint parameters in the local proof.

contents.name: The least purification environment dimension is the density rank
contents.support: §2.5.5 gives the dimension-r purification route; the local proof supplies the lower bound for all finite auxiliary spaces.
